definition: Dynamic Algorithm Configuration (DAC) changes algorithm parameters or components during execution using a learned policy. It replaces fixed heuristics with state-dependent decisions that can adapt as the search or optimization process evolves.
intuition: The best setting can change during a run, so a policy observes algorithm state and chooses the next configuration or component.
advantages: Adapts decisions to the current state of a running algorithm.
Can replace brittle hand-designed parameter schedules with learned policies.

limitations: A policy that works for one workload may not generalize to another.
Learning a policy requires state definitions, trajectories, and a reliable reward or cost signal.
